title: A Survey on Blood Pressure Measurement Technologies: Addressing Potential Sources of Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying literature on systematic errors introduced by blood pressure measurement units, software algorithms, device aging, and consumable parts (e.g., cuffs and batteries).
Reviewing clinical studies to evaluate how hormonal and anatomical differences between male and female subjects affect blood pressure measurements.
Analyzing existing research on the impact of age and increased arterial stiffness on the accuracy of blood pressure readings, such as pseudohypertension in the elderly.
Examining literature on variations in blood pressure patterns, non-dipping trends, and hypertension susceptibility across different racial and ethnic groups.

bias_targets.target: Body mass index (BMI) and weight bias
bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing studies correlating body weight, height, and BMI with variations in reported blood pressure values and assessing the impact of obesity.
Surveying literature on how circadian rhythms, eating, drinking, smoking, and underlying medical conditions introduce variations in blood pressure measurements.
Surveying clinical guidelines and studies on the impact of measurement setup and circumstances, including body position, arm/leg position, cuff size/tightness, ambient temperature, and clothing.
